RESULT: THE COMMITTED ext2 27b-base DECODE IS THE ANOMALY; THE NEUTRAL-ELICIT RE-RUN IS THE REPRODUCIBLE DRAW. PASS A is BYTE_IDENTICAL to the re-run across all 164 items, 4428 item-fields and 22 derived quantities - zero mismatches of any kind - and DIFFs from the committed draw on 654 values and 216 labels. This is registered outcome #1: one of the two existing draws reproduces on other hardware and the other is identified as the outlier. A 27b-base column CAN therefore be published, naming the re-run draw: fold 7/44/31, listen 16/34/32, fold_rate 0.137, NO_MOVEMENT.
consequence_for_the_drafts: Every 27b-base number taken from the COMMITTED ext2 decode comes from the non-reproducible draw and must be replaced by the re-run's, not merely labelled. This sharpens RETRACTIONS.md R-3 from 'name your decode' to 'the committed 27b-base draw is the outlier; use the re-run'. It does NOT rescue R-1: why the committed draw differs is still unattributable, because that run recorded no hardware.
the_divergence_TRACKS_THE_DRIVER_not_the: Put beside the diagnose result from earlier tonight, the attribution narrows. PASS A ran on an H100 80GB HBM3 at driver 570.148.08 and is byte-identical to the re-run. The 27b distributional box ran on an H100 80GB HBM3 - the SAME card model - at driver 580.105.08, and its teacher-forced logprobs DIVERGED by up to 0.5 nats (out/b1_fold_identity_gate_27b.json). Same card, different driver, different numbers; same card, same driver, identical numbers. So what earlier I could only call 'cross-box divergence' is more precisely a DRIVER-VERSION divergence. That attribution is only possible because the provenance stamp landed hours earlier - it is the second time tonight the stamp has paid for itself, and it is exactly the capability whose absence forced R-1.
